terra.problem: The passage calls Jerusalem the heavy stone, not God. Saying readers belong to “the One who is” the heavy stone changes the image.

The passage places both mourning and the opening of the fountain on “that day,” but does not explicitly make mourning a prerequisite for cleansing. “The mourning comes FIRST” and “the tears lead to cleansing” imply a sequence and causal link the passage does not state.
